summary: Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and held a post as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Anand A. Yang works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Swarthmore College (~1966–1970) and the University of Virginia (~1970–1976), he held positions at Sweet Briar College (~1974–1975), the University of Utah (1975), and the University of Washington (~2002).

Anand Venkatkrishnan works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, completing a doctoral thesis at Columbia University in 2015. He was a Junior Research Fellow at Balliol College, Oxford (attested 2016–2017) and an Assistant Professor at the University of Chicago (attested 2024–2026).

Ananda Guruge worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Ceylon (-1947) and the University of London. He held posts at the National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration, California State University, Fullerton, and University of the West.

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at Wycliffe College, University College London, and the University of London under Caroline Rhys Davids. He directed Ceylon's Mineral Survey and served at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), Professor at Patna University (~1949–1957), and Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

Anantalal Thakur worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Calcutta under several teachers. He held posts at the Mithila Institute (~1952–1975), the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971), and the University of Burdwan (~1975–1981).

Anantanand Rambachan works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of the West Indies, under Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds, later becoming an Emeritus Professor at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).

Anantasharma B. G. works in Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from National Sanskrit University, University of Madras, S-VYASA, and Central Sanskrit University. He served as Head at Veda Vijnana Shodha Samsthana, Chairperson at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, and Assistant Professor at Chanakya University.

Ananya Vajpeyi works in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, University of Oxford, and University of Chicago. Her appointments include posts at Columbia University and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.

Anastasiya Lozhkina specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (2007–2009) and Moscow State University (2009–2018), becoming a Junior Research Fellow at the Russian Academy of Sciences in 2018.

Anatol Waag studied linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies at the University of Leipzig (~1927–1931) under Johannes Hertel. He served as an Assistant at Leipzig (1932–1939), Lecturer in German at the University of Zagreb, and at Institut für Deutsche Volkskunde.
Anatoli Guenko studied under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay and Boris Turayev.
Anders Hilding Andersson was an Indology scholar who completed his M.A. (~1871–1875) and Ph.D. (~1875–1878) at Lund University, where he was appointed Docent of Greek Literature in 1879.

Andrea Acri is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Leiden University under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, after studying with Raffaele Torella. He held posts at Leiden, the EPHE, and EFEO.

Andrea Marion Pinkney works in Indology and religious studies. Attested as a Ph.D. candidate at Columbia University in 2007, she held posts as an Assistant Professor at the National University of Singapore (attested 2012) and McGill University (attested 2014–2018).

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2004–2010). Her posts include IUPUI and Indiana University Bloomington, where she became a full professor in 2021.

Andrea Schlosser works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her degrees from the Free University of Berlin (-2014) and studied under Richard G. Salomon and Ingo Strauch, later holding positions at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Andreas Bock-Raming is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Paul Hacker and held a post in Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeit at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Andreas Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, studied under several traditional Rinpoche teachers, and held a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
